To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Mobile apps for science learning offer a number of similar mobile app design features, (2) Many of the studies cite a specific theoretical foundation (most commonly situated learning theory) and apply this to the design and implementation of the mobile learning environments, and (3) The most common measured outcomes were students' basic scientific concepts or knowledge.

mobile apps for learning science offer a number of similar features, including technologybased scaffolding, location aware functionality, visual/audio representation, digital knowledge construction tools, digital knowledge sharing mechanisms, and differentiated role.

the design of mobile learning environments should include the use of technology to scaffold learning, location-aware functionality to enhance learning through real-world experiences, visual and audio representations to enhance learning through multiple representations, digital knowledge construction tools to support learning, digital knowledge sharing mechanisms to enhance collaboration, and differentiated roles to enhance learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a learning environment that supports students in the construction of knowledge about scientific phenomena.
the design of mobile learning environments for science learning.
the use of mobile apps for science teaching and learning, with an emphasis on how the design of mobile science apps can be informed by research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a lack of evidence to support the effectiveness of mobile learning apps in science education.
mobile apps for learning in science are still in their infancy, with much research yet to be done.
mobile apps for learning science have a lot of potential, and there are many different ways in which they can be used to support science learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mobile learning environment can be designed to facilitate learning in the sciences.
mobile learning is a powerful tool for science learning, especially when the mobile learning environment is well designed.

we have been working on the following: - Mobile learning and science - Mobile learning and social studies - Mobile learning and math - Mobile learning and reading comprehension - Mobile learning and vocabulary - Mobile learning and language acquisition - Mobile learning and writing
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of mobile learning environments for science education is still in its early phases.
mobile apps can be a useful tool for learning, but that the design features of mobile apps are often not well aligned with the underlying theories that are cited as their basis.
mobile apps are a powerful tool for science learning and that they can be used to enhance learning in many ways.
